title: Alibaba defrauded shareholders by concealing ties to suspected spy in Nvidia scandal, lawsuit says
html:
Alibaba inflated its share price by knowingly and materially understating in its 2024, 2025 and 2026 annual reports the risks that actual or suspected export control violations could harm its business, the proposed class action says.

PHOTO: REUTERS

AI generated

NEW YORK – Alibaba was sued on Nov 19 in New York by shareholders who accused the Chinese e-commerce giant of defrauding them by concealing its ties to the suspected Chinese spy whose relationship with former Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang contributed to his resignation last week.

According to a proposed class action filed in Manhattan federal court, Alibaba inflated its share price by knowingly and materially understating in its 2024, 2025 and 2026 annual reports the risks that actual or suspected export control violations could harm its business.

Shareholders cited Alibaba’s relationship with Megaspeed, a ​Singaporean company suspected of helping Beijing gain access to advanced Nvidia AI chips, and whose executive Alice Huang had a relationship with Jensen Huang.

The shareholders said Alibaba shares fell 14% over four days last week because of media reports on Alibaba’s ties to Alice Huang and Megaspeed, including that Alibaba had become Megaspeed’s “dominant” customer.

They attributed part of the decline to a Nov 12 Reuters article that said Nvidia’s spy scandal could spur Washington to tighten restrictions on Chinese AI companies’ remote use of advanced processors.

Alibaba did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Eddie Wu, its chief executive, is also a defendant.

Nvidia faces several shareholder lawsuits over the spy scandal, including allegations of lax oversight by its directors.

Wu said on Nov 19 that Alibaba remained on track for US$100 billion (S$129 billion) in external cloud revenue and a 20% earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) margin by 2030, despite US curbs on access to computing power that could affect the company’s products and services in 2027. The restrictions were imposed after Huang resigned from Nvidia.

In June, Alibaba sued the US government over being added to a blacklist of “Chinese military companies” that the US Department of Defense linked to China’s military.

In October, a federal judge in California granted Alibaba an injunction barring the US government from denying Pentagon ​contracts to firms whose lobbyists also work with designated Chinese military companies. Alibaba said that restriction caused its lobbyists to retreat as they feared losing other clients, and violated its First Amendment constitutional right to speak to and petition the government.

The Nov 19 lawsuit by Alibaba shareholder Withida Bihan seeks unspecified damages for holders of Alibaba’s American depositary shares between May 23, 2024, and Nov 11, 2026. REUTERS
summary: The shareholders said Alibaba shares fell 14% over four days last week because of media reports on its ties to Alice Huang and Megaspeed.
